title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried chicken with peanuts and dried chillies
excerpt: The celebrated Sichuan stir-fry: small pieces of marinated chicken cooked with dried red chillies, Sichuan pepper, and peanuts in a tangy sweet-and-sour sauce. Fast to cook and fiercely flavourful.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kung Pao chicken (Gōngbǎo jīdīng) is a Sichuan dish named after Ding Baozhen (1820 to 1886), a Qing Dynasty official who held the title Gōngbǎo (palace guardian) and who was said to have loved this dish. It spread internationally as one of the gateway dishes of Chinese cooking in the West, often in Americanised versions with a sweeter, cornstarch-heavy sauce. The authentic Sichuan version is drier than the Chinese-American adaptation, with a clear sweet-sour-salty-numbing balance and relatively small amounts of sauce coating the ingredients rather than pooling. Dried Tianjin or facing-heaven chillies are traditional; they provide flavour and colour more than heat, though they do contribute some.

recipeTools.notes: A wok or large frying pan.

content.text: Velvet the chicken with cornflour and egg white before marinating: this step produces the silky, tender texture that defines restaurant-quality stir-fried chicken. Have everything cut, measured, and ready before you heat the wok: stir-frying moves very quickly and there is no time to prepare once cooking starts. The wok must be very hot before anything goes in.

items.preparation: 1 tbsp for velveting chicken; 1 tbsp for the sauce
whole dried red chillies; seeds shaken out

content.text: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of cornflour, the egg white, and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes. Mix the sauce: combine the remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, shaoxing wine, sugar, sesame oil, and 1 tablespoon of cornflour dissolved in 2 tablespoons of water.

Heat the oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through and lightly coloured. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.

Pour in the sauce and toss everything together for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken. Add the peanuts and spring onion and toss for a further 30 seconds. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
